name: heart failure overview
title: Heart failure decision chart: confirm with natriuretic peptide, ECG and echo, then sort the unstable patient by congestion (wet or dry) and perfusion (warm or cold) into acute treatment, and the stable patient by ejection fraction into reduced (diuretic, triple therapy, then ARNI, ivabradine, SGLT2 inhibitor and devices in order) or preserved (diuretics and risk factors)

root.title: Breathless, edematous, tired: is it HEART FAILURE (HF), and is the patient UNSTABLE now?
lines: a syndrome: typical symptoms + structural heart disease · the ejection fraction (EF) is not needed to diagnose it
1 · natriuretic peptide (BNP): LOW rules HF out  →  2 · ECG: normal makes reduced EF very unlikely  →  3 · ECHO, the gold standard: EF

groups.title: ACUTE decompensated: is it WET (congested)? is it COLD (hypoperfused)?
lines: WARM + DRY: adjust the oral therapy · look for the trigger: infection, anemia, thyroid, ischemia

groups.title: CHRONIC: what is the EF on echo?
lines: New York Heart Association (NYHA) class: I no symptoms · II mild
III comfortable only at rest · IV symptoms at rest
every drug: start LOW, double every 2–4 weeks, check K+ and creatinine
